ai.description: Boulenger’s Dasia reaches 15 cm snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with dark crossbands and a distinct bluish-grey belly. Key features include smooth scales and a prehensile tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dasia subcaerulea* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale vertebral stripe that contrasts sharply with its olive-brown dorsal coloration.
ai.habitat: Boulenger's Dasia inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in high-canopy trees at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Boulenger's Dasia is primarily arboreal and diurnal, spending its active hours foraging for insects and small invertebrates within the forest canopy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dasia subcaerulea* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from April to July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dasia subcaerulea* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,200 meters.
